data.content_ref: inline:The discrete-bundle interpretation (buy 3 groups of 7 at $2 each) and the continuous unit-rate interpretation (multiply 21 by $2/7) are not equivalent reductions; they contradict at the level of mechanism even though they agree at the level of numerical output. The bundle model depends on integer divisibility of the target by 7; the continuous model does not. The equivalence is refuted if the target quantity is not a multiple of 7 (e.g., 10 pencils), where the bundle model forces a remainder or an overbuy and the continuous model does not, exposing them as logically distinct principles whose convergence at 21 is accidental, not structural.
